title: Ch3.7 · Common table expressions
summary: Name a statement-scoped intermediate result and compose readable multi-step queries.
objectives: Explain the scope of a CTE
Separate an intermediate relation from a stored view
Use a CTE to make a multi-stage query auditable

sections.title: Common table expressions
sections.body: A CTE names a temporary relation for one statement. It improves the reasoning surface of a query without changing the stored schema or creating persistent data.

sourceLens.whyExaminable: This unit is split directly from the supplied Chapter 3 lecture deck so retrieval and mistake repair stay topic-sized.

examples.title: Compute department totals in one CTE, then compare each total with the average of those totals in a second query step.
steps: A CTE names a temporary relation for one statement. It improves the reasoning surface of a query without changing the stored schema or creating persistent data.

math.name: CTE scope
math.purpose: Use it to mark an intermediate relation that exists only for one statement.
math.explanation: The name T is available to the statement that follows WITH and is not a permanent relation.
